[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — renewal status, capacity ask, EU region add-on, and next steps. emily, want to kick off with where you are on usage and what's prompting this now?

[00:40] Raj: and timing is tight — marketing ran pilots and now legal/procurement wants a clean set of security docs and a SLA before approving a spend increase.
[00:55] Aisha: understood. benji, can you summarize the performance differences we saw on our side for host vs dedicated?
[01:05] Benji: sure — so hosted is easiest to start, but with current qps the variance is higher. Dedicated gives predictable throughput, lower p95 latency because we can tune batch sizes and KV cache locality. on our benchmarks a dedicated c5-config (sorry, internal naming) gave about 20-30% lower p95 on 2k tokens versus hosted at similar cost when you account for caching. caveat, of course, depends on seq lengths and concurrency.
[01:35] Dr. Emily: that's interesting. latency at p95 is important for triage UX. what's the incremental cost of doubling capacity in dedicated vs hosted credits?
[01:48] Aisha: i'll put numbers in the quote. high level: dedicated has a commit but you get better unit economics for sustained load. hosted scales but per-token is higher. we'll send a revised quote that compares both options side-by-side.
[02:02] Sophie: procurement wants to see the breakouts — per-token, reserved commit, and any termination clauses. also can you show EU region pricing?
[02:12] Aisha: yes — we'll include EU region add-on line items.
[02:16] Liam: from infra — we're also evaluating VPC/private deployment for PHI concerns; is private deployment required for EU residency or can we do region isolation with Redwood Private?
[02:28] Benji: good question. region isolation can be done with hosted + region pinning for most customers, but for strict PHI controls we often recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated in a VPC with KMS integration. private does add ops overhead and licensing; we can map the controls in the SOC2/KMS docs.
[02:45] Raj: is the KMS/HSM integration supported for EU keys? we need keys to be EU-controlled ideally.
[02:51] Benji: yes, we support customer-managed keys in supported regions; i'll add specifics in the security bundle.
[03:00] Aisha: quick poll — are you leaning dedicated + EU or hosted + EU?
[03:05] Dr. Emily: leaning dedicated + EU for predictability and easier performance SLAs.
[03:10] Sophie: procurement would prefer hosted if it's significantly cheaper, but security is the gating item.
[03:16] Aisha: fair. one thing to consider — we can do a short benchmark on dedicated capacity to show p95 improvements; that often helps procurement justify the commit. benji, can you run a bench for their seq profiles?
[03:28] Benji: yes — i'll prepare a test matrix. i'm thinking two runs: one at 2k tokens focusing on triage, one at 4k for long notes. include concurrency 8 and 16, and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:43] Dr. Emily: that'll be perfect. also want to validate model variants — quantized vs fp16 — because we need consistent output quality. any quality regressions could be a blocker.
[03:56] Benji: we'll run both model variants and include rouge/bleu-ish metrics plus a small hand review set you provide. we won't rely only on automated metrics.
[04:08] Sophie: on legal — contract extension length? we're thinking 12 months if pricing is acceptable. any discounts for multiyear?
[04:17] Aisha: standard is 12 months for renewals, we can propose a 10% discount on reserved commit for 12-month upfront vs 0% for month-to-month; for multiyear we have a different tier — we can outline in the quote.
[04:31] Raj: timeline — procurement needs security docs and benchmarking evidence before vendor selection, ideally within two weeks.
[04:36] Maya: i'll share SOC2 artifacts, the data residency whitepaper, and the KMS integration doc after this call.
[04:42] Dr. Emily: thanks. question — how do you handle audit logs and access controls? who sees PII in logs?
[04:50] Benji: we redact PII at ingress in most deployments, we have audit logs with RBAC, and logs can be routed to customer-managed SIEM. full details in the security bundle.
[05:01] Sophie: procurement also needs a standard BAA/DP agreement for PHI — do you have a template?
[05:06] Aisha: yes we have BAA templates; i'll include that and flag legal to be ready to iterate.
[05:12] Raj: any potential black swan of availability if we go dedicated in EU? like maintenance windows that would impact SLAs?
[05:20] Benji: dedicated clusters have maintenance windows but we offer redundancy and cross-zone failover; we'll show expected uptime and escalation procedures in the SLA section.
[05:30] Dr. Emily: one more — can we get sample telemetry / cost dashboards so our finance team sees projected monthly spend?
[05:37] Maya: yes, we'll share the Console screenshots and a sample cost forecast for 2x capacity and EU add-on.
[05:44] Sophie: on procurement, any minimum notice for capacity changes? we might want the ability to burst during marketing pushes.
[05:51] Aisha: we have burst options; dedicated can be configured with burst capacity or autoscale policies — we'll include that in the quote.
[06:00] Raj: what's the rollback plan if quality regressions appear after we switch a model or quantize?
[06:06] Benji: Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a previous model variant. we also support evaluation suites to detect regressions pre-rollout.
[06:16] Dr. Emily: ok good. so next steps recap?
[06:20] Aisha: i'll list: Aisha to send revised commercial including 2x capacity, dedicated vs hosted comparison, EU region pricing and burst options; Benji to run the benchmark tests; Maya to share security and residency docs; Sophie/Raj to confirm procurement timeline.
[06:36] Sophie: yes, and we'll get back on legal questions once we see the BAA and SLA.
[06:42] Aisha: great. any other questions from the team?
[06:45] Liam: one minor — latency SLO target we're asking for is p95 < 350ms for 2k tokens, is that something achievable?
[06:53] Benji: p95 < 350ms for 2k tokens is aggressive but achievable on dedicated with the right instance type and caching; we'll validate in the benchmark.
[07:03] Dr. Emily: sounds good. thanks everyone. we'll wait for the docs and the benchmark plan.
[07:10] Aisha: thanks — we'll target sending the quote and docs by oct 22 and schedule the benchmark for the week of oct 27. end call.
